criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The mission need, benefit to Australia, operator, user needs, goal and measurable preliminary requirements are clearly connected. Relevant references are provided. A minor weakness is that the 10 m resolution and weekly cloud-free coverage requirements are not yet validated against the imaging method or feasible orbit.

evidence.quote: Give reef managers direct, repeatable observations of coral colour over the whole Great Barrier Reef
Its customers are the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority
Deliver each image to an Australian ground station within 24 hours of capture.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: The Gantt chart is detailed and mission-sequenced, with completed/planned work, deadlines, float, explicit risks and contingencies, and relevant information sources. The plan connects orbit work to imaging and communications needs. Some task duration and milestone detail remains broad, but the project appears feasible.

evidence.quote: Project work is divided into weeks in the Gantt chart in Figure 1
Week 10 is float as well as editing time: no new design work is planned in it.
Table 2 lists the sources I plan to use and what each is for.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: The submission includes useful orbital calculations, a preliminary coverage assessment, interpretation of the main feasibility trade, and evidence of an STK scenario. This is meaningful early design progress, though there are no simulation results or sensor/coverage validation yet.

evidence.quote: I have also made first hand calculations for a candidate orbit, a circular sun-synchronous orbit at 600 km altitude
A first STK scenario with this orbit has been set up, and its period agrees with the hand calculation.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report has a logical structure, clear headings, labelled figures and tables, and a mostly professional style with a reference list. The Gantt chart and tables are legible and useful. Some wording is informal or awkward, and several references are broad or incompletely specified, so presentation is not fully polished.

technical_issues.issue: The 60 km swath is inferred from 6,000 pixels at 10 m sampling, but no sensor focal-plane, field-of-view, altitude, or image-quality constraints justify that pixel count or swath.

The 2,700 km ground-track spacing is an approximate equatorial same-day separation, not a complete revisit or weekly coverage analysis; orbit phasing, latitude, target geometry, daylight, clouds, and off-nadir imaging are not assessed.
The 10 m resolution and weekly cloud-free imaging requirements are stated as preliminary targets but are not yet supported by evidence that they suffice to detect bleaching using the cited method.

overall: A strong preliminary report with a well-motivated Australian mission, a detailed and risk-aware project plan, and credible initial orbit work. The main next step is to validate sensor assumptions and quantify target revisit and coverage in STK.

feedback.summary: You present a well-motivated Australian reef-monitoring mission, a detailed and risk-aware project plan, and credible initial orbit work. Your next step is to turn the preliminary imaging and orbit assumptions into validated sensor and target-coverage results, while polishing the evidence and presentation.
next_steps: In Preliminary Progress, justify the 6,000-pixel assumption with sensor focal-plane, field-of-view, altitude and image-quality constraints; use these to verify the 60 km swath and whether 10 m imagery can detect bleaching using your cited method.

Extend the STK analysis beyond the approximate 2,700 km equatorial same-day spacing: assess revisit and weekly coverage for target locations, including orbit phasing, latitude, daylight, clouds and off-nadir limits, and report the results.

In Project Plan and Figure 1, retain your contingencies but specify broad task durations and milestones more precisely. In Information sources, complete reference details, and edit informal or awkward wording for a more polished report.

criteria.C1: Mission Concept & Rationale clearly connects the reef-monitoring need, Australian benefit, user and measurable targets; the GBRMPA user and 24-hour delivery requirement are specific strengths. To reach the highest standard, validate the 10 m and weekly cloud-free targets against the cited bleaching method and feasible coverage.
criteria.C2: Project Plan and Figure 1 provide a mission-sequenced Gantt chart with float, risks and contingencies; Information sources links sources to their purpose. For a stronger plan, make broad task durations and milestones more precise while keeping the plan tied to mission needs.
criteria.C3: Preliminary Progress includes useful hand calculations for a 600 km sun-synchronous orbit and an STK scenario whose period agrees with the calculation. Build on this by validating the 60 km swath and quantifying target revisit and weekly coverage in STK.
criteria.C4: The report is logically structured, with clear headings and useful labelled figures and tables. To polish presentation, revise informal or awkward wording and ensure references are complete and consistently specified.
